new_jobs.title: Closing Receptionist / Evening Operations Coordinator (Seasonal)
new_jobs.description:
**Employer:** Valley Christmas Lights

**Type:** W\-2, Full\-Time (40 hrs/week), fully remote\- **must be based in the United States** **Schedule:** Tuesday–Saturday, 11:30 AM – 8:00 PM **Arizona time**

**Start:** September 23rd\- trained and running solo before the October install season opens

Mission

Be the customer's last call of the day and the crew's first advantage tomorrow.

You run the afternoon and evening phones, send quotes to homeowners who reach out after hours, and answer every customer question that lands while the office is quiet. Then, before you log off, you close the day: every job on tomorrow's board is briefed and correct, every dollar billable today is collected, every time card is punched out and accurate, and every crew walks into tomorrow morning knowing exactly what they're doing and what they need. Nothing rolls into tomorrow half\-done.

Outcomes (what "great" looks like)

* No call goes unanswered during your coverage window, and no evening voicemail sits overnight.
* Quotes go out the same hour they're requested, not the next morning.
* Every job on the next day's schedule has a complete, accurate brief before you log off\- address, scope, access details, materials, crew assignment\- confirmed with the customer.
* Daily billing is collected and reconciled at close.
* Every time card for the day is punched out and correct, with any correction documented and confirmed.
* Crew leads start each morning without a single question that could have been answered the night before.
* Leadership can look at the next day's board at 8:05 PM and trust it completely.

Core Responsibilities1\. Phones \& Customer Service (Primary, all shift)

You are the front line for the entire afternoon and evening.

* **Live answering.** Pick up inbound calls within 3 rings during your coverage window. When you can't, return the voicemail or text within 3 minutes. Warm, calm, professional tone\- many of these callers are choosing between us and two competitors on the same afternoon.
* **Lead qualification \& booking.** Ask structured questions to determine service type (seasonal vs. permanent lighting), property type (roof height, size, features), and timeline. Book quotes and installs directly with accurate details.
* **Customer questions, all of them.** Pricing, scheduling, what's included, what happens if a strand goes out in December, when takedown happens, where the deposit went. You are the answer, not the router!
* **Service issues.** If a customer reports a problem, schedule a fix for the next day.
* **CRM hygiene.** Every call, text, and email logged. Every status current. Nothing from a personal phone or personal email, ever.

2\. Remote Quoting

* Take address and square footage from inbound leads and produce a priced quote with a visual mockup using our quoting tool.
* Send it by email and text with a clear next step.
* Follow up on your own quotes through our defined cadence until the customer books or declines.
* **You own the after\-hours window.** Our daytime quoting team is off at 5:00 PM Arizona. From 5:00 to 8:00, which is when a lot of homeowners actually sit down and fill out forms, the quote either goes out from you or it doesn't go out.

3\. The Day\-Close

**Tomorrow's briefs.**

* Pull every job on the next day's schedule and verify each one is complete and correct: address, scope of work, roofline count and details, color and product selections, special requests, gate codes, pets, parking and ladder access, power outlet locations, and any note the customer added since booking.
* Confirm the crew assignment on every job and that the assigned crew can see it.
* Confirm materials and equipment for each job are accounted for so nothing gets discovered at 7:00 AM.
* Flag anything incomplete or contradictory to the install lead **tonight**, not tomorrow.

**Today's billing.**

* Collect balances due on every job completed today. Run the card on file, send the payment link, make the call — whatever it takes to close it out the same day.
* Verify deposits collected on jobs booked today.
* Reconcile the day: what was invoiced, what was collected, what's outstanding and why.
* Escalate anything you can't collect with the reason, same day.

**Today's time cards.**

* Confirm every crew member is punched out. Chase down anyone who forgot before you close the day and get their timecard corrected.
* Review the day's hours against the job schedule and flag anything that doesn't reconcile.
* **Corrections follow the documented process, every time:** note what was changed, why, and get the crew member's confirmation. We do not adjust anyone's recorded hours silently. Our payroll is tied to hours and to installed revenue, and Arizona requires us to keep accurate daily records for four years. This is the single most compliance\-sensitive task in the role, and we will train you on it specifically.

**Set the crews up.**

* Send the end\-of\-day rundown: tomorrow's jobs, crew assignments, anything unusual, anything that changed.
* Communicate any late reschedule, cancellation, or add to the crews affected.
* Note anything the morning shift needs to pick up.

4\. Daily Handoff

* Start of shift: read the opening receptionist's handoff and pick up anything open.
* End of shift: send a short close\-out\- calls answered, voicemails returned, quotes sent, leads booked, billing collected and outstanding, time card exceptions, tomorrow's board confirmed clean, and anything needing leadership's decision.

Qualifications

**Required**

* 2\+ years in reception, scheduling, dispatch, inside sales, or admin support\- ideally somewhere with a real phone volume.
* **Located in the United States.** This role must be W\-2, and we need US employment eligibility.
* Clear, warm phone presence. You'll be the voice of the company for the entire evening.
* Strong written communication\- a large share of customer contact is text and email.
* Genuinely organized, and specifically the kind of organized t
